entries.grounds: `required` (adapters.py:197) goes to three places: review_ocr.coverage(), whose first statement is `required = sorted(set(required))` (review_ocr.py:80; `missing`, `excluded`, `absent` and the reasons are built from that copy, :118-130); review_ocr.findings() `set(required)` (:144, membership for `in_scope` at :156); and the session record (adapters.py:249-250 -> run.py:497 `sessions=[...]` -> RUN.json). The mutant hands git's own row order on. That order equals sorted() for every path whose bytes decode without replacement (tree order is the byte order of the full names, code-point order for valid UTF-8; measured here: 800 random trees with file/directory conflicts between base and head, `git diff -z --name-status --no-renames`, 0 differences from sorted()). It differs only where bytes and decoded text disagree (an invalid UTF-8 byte is decoded with errors='replace', workspace.py:71, e.g. b'\xff' -> U+FFFD sorts after U+FFFE which git's bytes put before it): one list in RUN.json is then ordered differently. No product code reads that order (verify.py reads RUN.json keys other than `sessions`: story_outcomes, story_errors, budget, usage, no_progress, productproof, delivery_verdict, final_main, journal, settings). The tests that read the list compare it with sorted(...) or a literal and pass on the mutant because git's order equals sorted() for their valid names, not because order is unread: test_v21_defects_ocrz.py:90,98,110,124; test_v21_kills3_T10c.py:193,221; test_v21_defects_ocr.py:127,163; only test_v21_review_chain.py:387 is order-free. Hence AUDITED, not EQUIVALENT.

entries.grounds: The line (cli.py:101-103, the only producer) is printed to stderr after the run and its evidence are complete: `aisef run: the anchor was NOT written to <path> (<Class>: <text>); keep the printed one`.
